doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: Named YES on the 7 May 2026 budget (7.28 overall / 9.34 residential). "They want to protect the things that we love in the city." No cap, formula or glide path. Against interest, added pass 2: on 24 Nov 2025 he moved to reduce the infrastructure allocation from 5.5M to 4M dollars to help hold the rate, carried 7–2 — a restraint action, but on capital renewal, not a rule on the residential rate.

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: Started OUR DWTN and supported the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan. No Public Order Team, no 6am–10pm bylaw hours. Added pass 2: moved with Coun. Thompson the derelict-and-neglected-buildings motion carried unanimously 23 Jul 2026 — "This is especially important in the downtown core, where we've seen some prominent buildings sit empty for many years." That is a property-condition instrument, not a public-order one.

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "We need to get back on track and speed up new rental, affordable, social and market housing. I commit to making that happen as soon as possible." No unit target and no 25/20/15/30 composition mix. Record: named YES on Missing Middle, 26 Jan 2023.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: Authorized 2026 re-election site with a policies page (eight themes) plus a Record page, both with published lastmod dates. Directional, not costed: no tax formula, no permit benchmark, no dashboard, no 25M-dollar threshold. /endorsements says only "More coming soon…" and /yourvision is a contact form, not a platform.

cells.quote: We need to get back on track and speed up new rental, affordable, social and market housing. I commit to making that happen as soon as possible.
cells.why: Commits to a supply mix with no unit target and no composition share. M6 asks for 12,000+ net new homes and stacked shares of 25% missing middle / 20% three-bedroom / 15% non-market / 30% purpose-built rental; none of the four appears. Record, matching, not a second mark: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023; Family Housing Policy (3-bedroom incentive) on the Record page. Added pass 2, Record context: his 6 Dec 2025 open letter to View Royal — "Build housing, stop complaining!" — states Victoria "has approved over 7,000 housing units this term and is ahead of provincial targets." That is a volume claim from before his 31 Dec 2025 declaration, so it is Record, not a 2026 campaign sentence, and it still carries no composition share. The 9,000-units figure is campaign-attributed and is not stamped.

That motion is scored as Record on row 30 and as the sourced miss on row 28. The 2023–25 "lowest municipal tax increase of most surrounding major cities" line is a comparative frame, not a restraint instrument, and is not scored.

cells.why: Commits: he moved the motion with Coun. Thompson and it carried unanimously 23 Jul 2026, directing staff to report back on strengthening bylaws and enforcement tools for derelict and neglected properties, to scan comparable municipalities, and to assess whether provincial legislative change is needed. Comparable instrument to M71's existing levers (vacant property licensing, conditions on business-licence renewal) and to M71's advocacy for provincial enabling legislation to surcharge persistent commercial vacancies. Not Aligned: no 11%-to-5% vacancy target, no quarterly vacancy report by block and sector, no employment-lands no-net-loss rule, and the motion is a report-back rather than the lever itself. Context, not a second mark: home-page "More supports for local business and tourism"; Record-page downtown tax-reduction, facade and Douglas Street funds. OUR DWTN cleanliness is row 26. No sourced miss on this cluster, so Close is allowed.

cells.what: tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: Commits, same instrument, on the M64 indoor-heat limb.
cells.why: Dell moved the motion with Couns. Thompson and Caradonna in May 2026; the resulting staff direction was approved unanimously 23 Jul 2026 and directs staff to report back on amendments to the City's Rental Property Standards of Maintenance Bylaw ensuring no prohibition of cooling devices in rental units, including passive cooling. The Program names that instrument in the same words: M64's first ordered step is to "ban unreasonable landlord prohibition of portable cooling, if the Standards of Maintenance Bylaw or the business-licence power can carry it." Same bylaw, same prohibition-on-the-prohibition, and the Program's 26°C performance rule is itself gated to a solicitor's hook — so a legal-feasibility direction is the Program's own step at this stage, not a substitute for it. 2026 campaign sentence, context, not a second mark: "we must accelerate construction of non-market housing, build thousands of new rental units, and strengthen policies to protect renters." Record, matching: Tenant Protection Bylaw; 30 Jul 2026 council unanimously enhanced displacement compensation. FLAG 1 — cluster: M9b short-term-rental licensing is entirely absent and M9's demoviction package is Record rather than a 2026 promise; a reader who scores the cluster rather than the instrument holds this at Close 2.0. FLAG 2 — accuracy, and it is the cap question: in his 30 Jul 2026 Facebook post Dell wrote that council gave renters "the strongest protections in the Province" and that "the City also hired a Tenant Protection Coordinator." The vote was unanimous, the largest enhancement was Hammond's amendment, and the City's own Tenant Relocation Guide has the coordinator appointed and paid by the applicant. That is an overstatement of his own role, not a vote contradicting a promise, so the incumbent cap is not applied here. If it is ruled a sourced miss, this cell caps at Partial+ 1.5.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls
cells.quote: Invest in streets, sidewalks & infrastructure.
cells.why: Commits to sidewalk and street investment. Neither: no sidewalk-gap inventory, no km-of-gap-closed figure, no crossing standard, no City-controlled transit-lever list. Sourced miss, added pass 2 — actions over words. On 24 Nov 2025 Dell moved to reduce the City's infrastructure allocation from 5.5M to 4M dollars, carried 7–2; Victoria Buzz reports the reduction could affect "roadwork, the city's fleet, parks' infrastructure, and playgrounds." M20b states that sidewalk and crossing construction is "a named allocation inside M25… not new capital" — that is, inside the very envelope he moved to cut. The 2026 promise sits under the action as context. Cap applied: this cell cannot exceed Partial+ 1.5; it scores Partial 1.0 on its own terms, so the cap does not bite. FLAG: a reader could hold the action to be a Disagrees and mark Weak 0.5 or Opposed −1.0; the add-back condition (restore if non-market-change revenue exceeded 1M dollars) and the budget-balancing context are why this pass does not.

cells.quote: Added pass 2. "Councillor Matt Dell put forth a motion to reduce the City's infrastructure funding from 5.5 million to 4 million dollars," with add-back "if any Non-Market Change (NMC) tax revenue comes in, in excess of 1 million, that it be added back into the infrastructure budget." Carried 7–2, 24 Nov 2025, during deliberations that were trying to bring the 2026 increase down toward 4%. M25 is a zero-net-new sequencing rule inside the existing envelope (11.5M major plus 3.5M local street rehabilitation in 2026), so a reduction of the envelope is a decision about M25's money without being a vote against M25's sequencing rule. Recorded here, scored as the sourced miss on row 28. No pothole report-to-fix standard and no published quarterly road-condition ranking. Adjacency rule applied: Record, not Opposed.

cells.quote: Added pass 2. On 7 Apr 2026 Dell moved, with Coun. Loughton, a 175,000-dollar grant to the Victoria Curling Club for a new ice plant, conditional on the club raising a further 75,000: "This money will help build community, keep seniors active, and ensure newcomers can learn to curl." Carried. M65 requires a line-by-line review of every grant and subsidy over 50,000 dollars a year against a published three-part test of jurisdiction, outcomes and duplication; this grant is three and a half times that threshold and no such test is cited, in a cycle whose draft plan required 8.38M dollars of cuts. Recorded, not scored: moving one grant is not a vote against the review process, and M65 is a process measure. No zero-based cycle, no grant test and no service-area rotation appears anywhere in his 2026 material. Budget-vote sentences are scored on row 13.

cells.quote: Added pass 2. On 3 Mar 2026 council voted 8–1 to discontinue the City's Urban Development Institute membership, on a motion arising from Coun. Hammond during budget deliberations; Dell was the single vote against ending it. Membership had risen 75% that year; ending it saved 2,625 dollars. In earlier September 2025 deliberations Dell said the City is "in the pocket of trying to build more housing in the city." Adjacency rule applied: this is Record, not Opposed. M79d's instrument is a searchable public registry of proponent meetings filed by the City side within 10 business days; a vote about the City's own membership dues in a development-industry association is not a vote against that registry, and marking it as one could not be defended to the candidate's face. No lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee abolition and no next-term-only remuneration rule appears in his 2026 material. Also recorded: he recused himself on 7 Dec 2023 (boulevard tax) and 11 Dec 2025 (letter to a provincial legislative committee) — recusals are process facts, not marks.
